newsitem.title: USA: Avista Energy sets power district alliance.
newsitem.headline: Avista Energy sets power district alliance.

text.p: Avista Energy said Tuesday it has formed an alliance with Chelan County Public Utility District to offer "real-time" trading of energy and joint marketing of commodity products and services.
The terms of the alliance make this announcement the first of its kind in the Northwest, according to Avista, Washington Water Power Co's renamed energy maketing enterprise.

Avista said the agreement allows it to market, on a "real-time" basis, a portion of the significant output from Chelan County's hydroelectric resources, and to jointly market energy products and services to other utilities in the region.

The district owns and operates the nation's second largest non-federal, publicly-owned hydroelectric generating system, which includes Rock Island and Rocky Reach dams on the Columbia River and Lake Chelan dam.

Under the agreement, Avista said, the alliance will assume responsibility for real-time sales of energy from the district's share of its hydropower resources. About 28 percent, or 557 megawatts, of the generating capacity of the dams will be available for real-time scheduling and resource optimization.

"Avista Energy will help identify and execute the short-term market transactions that will yield real benefits for both companies," President Lloyd Meyers said. "Chelan County PUD will continue to handle the long-term sales of its energy resources," he added.

Avista Energy also has an alliance with Mock Energy Services announced in November. Together, Avista Energy and Mock have access to more than 25 percent of California's direct-access natural gas business and jointly market electric commodity service, fuel oil, propane and other energy products to industrial and large commercial customers throughout California. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
